questions.concept: Presence expiry updates a live subscription through server-side state
questions.context:
Convex 1.41.0 and Presence 0.3.2. docHeartbeat delegates to presence.heartbeat, and whoIsViewing uses the line below. Alice is the only viewer in document A. Her tab sends a successful heartbeat with interval 400 ms, the subscription sees online:true, and the tab then stops all heartbeats without calling leave. Clients only subscribe: no polling, cleanup, or other client writes occur.

```ts
return await presence.list(ctx, roomToken);
```
questions.question: Once the component processes the missed-heartbeat timeout, what does the existing subscription receive?

options.text: No change until another viewer writes to the same document.
options.rationale: The component schedules its own persisted timeout transition; another client write is unnecessary.

options.text: The Alice entry disappears from the room list.
options.rationale: The tested component retains recently offline entries and changes online to false.

options.text: Periodic query results driven only by Date.now(), eventually showing Alice offline.
options.rationale: A wall-clock read does not itself invalidate a Convex subscription. The control query stayed unchanged after its deadline.

options.text: An updated list retaining Alice with online:false.
options.rationale: The scheduled component timeout changes persisted presence state, delivering the offline transition to the existing subscription.
